name: California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of California
city: California (session location not stated on the site)
what_you_do: You spend a week at a summer camp for 11th graders from across the state. You learn how city, county and state government work. You learn how elections run, and you write a bill.
grades: 11th grade (the site says each delegate is an 11th grade student during the 2026-27 school year)
who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade. A local American Legion Auxiliary Unit must pick and sponsor you. Each high school can send only one delegate. If no Unit sponsors your school, you can apply as a statewide alternate. No age rule is stated.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program pages. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22 to 27, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
deadline_text: 2027 (84th) session: dates and location not posted yet. The online form for Unit-selected 2027 delegates and alternates opens February 2027. The form for Department (statewide) alternate applicants opens April 2027. Last session: June 22 to 27, 2026.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor. Or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. The site has a list to find one. Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Many use a form, an essay or an interview. Picked students then fill out an online form. It opens in February 2027. Is there no Unit at your school? You can apply as a statewide alternate. That form opens in April 2027.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages. The 2027 session will be the 84th. Adult staff must be at least 20 or out of high school for at least three years, so staff roles are not for teens.
